subject: Invoice question: rounding on per-request aggregation causing overage
messages:
From: Sophie Patel <sophie.patel@avasolutions.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Solutions Billing <billing@avasolutions.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:12:00Z
Subject: Question on October invoice — apparent rounding overage

Hi Jonas,

Hope youre well. We received our October invoice (attached) and the usage_export file you provided. After reconciling against our internal metering, were seeing a persistent ~$320 discrepancy where our totals are lower than Redwoods invoice. It looks like small per-request rounding on token counts for streaming sessions is adding up when aggregated across ~1.2M calls.

Attachments: invoice_2026-10-31.pdf, usage_export_2026-10.csv

Can your team provide: 1) a line-by-line per-request export for the billing window (raw token counts before any rounding), or 2) an explanation of how you compute the billed token totals from streaming sessions? Our finance team needs this for month-end close and will likely request a credit if its an aggregation artifact.

Wed appreciate a response by Nov 9 if possible — our close is on Nov 11.

Thanks,
Sophie Patel
Finance Manager, Ava Solutions
Sophie.Patel@avasolutions.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Patel <sophie.patel@avasolutions.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Question on October invoice — apparent rounding overage

Hi Sophie,

Thanks for the note and for sending the invoice/exports. Were sorry for the trouble and totally understand the need to close this before Nov 11. Ive looped in Marissa from billing and Dylan from engineering so we can get you a forensic breakdown.

Initial plan:
- Dylan will pull a per-request raw metering extract (unrounded token counts) for the October window and a derived billed tally.
- Billing (Marissa) will run a reconciliation script that applies our aggregation/rounding rules so we can show a reconciled delta line-by-line.
- If this turns out to be an aggregation rounding artifact, well propose a credit amount and apply it in the November invoice with a note.

Can you confirm whether you need decimal-level precision in the export (e.g., fractional token totals) or if an integer-per-request export is fine for your audit team? Well aim to send the raw extract by EOD Nov 4.

Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Patel <sophie.patel@avasolutions.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Question on October invoice — apparent rounding overage

Hi Sophie + team,

I pulled a targeted sample and wanted to explain what Im seeing — attaching meter_sample for transparency.

Summary:
- Our service tracks streaming token deltas per chunk; each chunks token estimate is stored as a float internally. At billing time we apply a per-request rounding rule (round up to the nearest whole token) before aggregation.
- In your workload there are many short streaming chunks (~5-15 tokens) that get rounded up. Individually these are 0.4-0.6 token upward adjustments, which compound across large call volumes.

Example (sample row from metering_sample_202611.csv):
request_id: r_3891, raw_tokens: 4.6, billed_tokens: 5
request_id: r_3892, raw_tokens: 3.7, billed_tokens: 4
Aggregate over 1,200,345 requests -> billed delta = sum(ceil(raw)) - sum(raw) = ~320.75 tokens equivalent (billed units convert to $ after tiering).

Proposed next steps:
1) Run full window extraction of raw_tokens and billed_tokens (well provide CSV with three columns: request_id, raw_tokens, billed_tokens).
2) Compute the exact delta and present a credit amount. For transparency, wed also include the script we ran so your auditors can reproduce.

Ill upload the full export by EOD Nov 6 and attach the sample now.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Engineering (Metering)
Dylan.Brooks@redwood.com

From: Sophie Patel <sophie.patel@avasolutions.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Solutions Billing <billing@avasolutions.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T16:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Question on October invoice — apparent rounding overage

Thanks Dylan — that explanation makes sense and the sample matches what were seeing. We appreciate the transparency.

Two asks from finance: 1) please confirm the proposed credit amount and how it will be applied on our next invoice; 2) provide the per-request CSV and the script for our auditors. We need the credit applied (or an interim billing hold) before our close on Nov 11, otherwise our AP team will delay payment.

If you can commit to sending the full export and a credit note by Nov 9 EOD well mark the account to release payment on schedule.

Thanks,
Sophie

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Patel <sophie.patel@avasolutions.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Question on October invoice — apparent rounding overage

Hi Sophie,

Thanks for the patience. Dylans export matched your internal totals when we applied your provided aggregation (you were right on the math). The full run shows the billed delta equals 320.75 billed token-equivalents which converts to a $320.75 credit on your account (no tiering adjustments in this case because the delta sits within your base tier).

What were doing:
- Credit note attached: credit_note_20261109.pdf (applies to Nov invoice).
- Per-request CSV uploaded to our shared Drive (link below) and script included so your auditors can reproduce.
- Marissa will post the credit to your account and remark the Nov invoice so your AP team can process payment as usual.

Related links: https://hubspot.redwood.com/contacts/DEAL-4837, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_metering_exports

Please reply to confirm youre happy with the credit and well finalize the posting. Apologies for the extra effort this caused — were also adding a telemetry flag to surface high-volume rounding drift in future windows.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
